summary: This study presents a comprehensive X-ray spectroscopic analysis of 642 quasars, obtained by cross-matching the XMM-Newton Serendipitous Source Catalog (DR11) with the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (DR16) quasar catalog. After stringent quality filtering and automated spectral reduction, we derived reliable photon indices ($Γ$) and intrinsic 2--10 keV X-ray luminosities. Using multiwavelength data, sources were classified into 561 radio-quiet (RQ) and 81 radio-loud (RL) quasars. We estimate the bolometric luminosity and Eddington ratio ($λ_{\mathrm{Edd}}$) from absorption-corrected X-ray measurements and virial black hole masses. Our primary objective is to establish and characterize the fundamental relationship between the photon index and Eddington ratio for RQ population. We find that RQ quasars exhibit systematically higher Eddington ratios, peaking at $\log λ_{\mathrm{Edd}} \approx -1.2$, and softer spectra with $Γ\approx 2.0$. A statistically significant positive correlation between $Γ$ and $λ_{\mathrm{Edd}}$ is detected in RQ quasars, supporting disk--corona coupling models. To validate our results within the broader context of AGN evolution, we further examine the dependence of $λ_{\mathrm{Edd}}$ on redshift ($z$) and black hole mass ($M_{\mathrm{BH}}$). For RQ quasars, $λ_{\mathrm{Edd}}$ increases with redshift and decreases with $M_{\mathrm{BH}}$, in strong agreement with recent results \cite{aggarwal2024evidence}, highlighting the universal nature of these accretion trends. By correlating spectral slope with accretion rate, this work provides new insights into the interplay between accretion physics, jet activity, and the cosmic evolution of quasars.

AI.tldr: Study of 642 X-ray quasars (561 RQ, 81 RL) from XMM-Newton/SDSS data, finding RQ quasars have softer spectra (Γ≈2.0) and higher Eddington ratios (log λ_Edd≈-1.2), with a significant positive Γ–λ_Edd correlation supporting disk–corona coupling, and λ_Edd increasing with redshift but decreasing with black hole mass.
AI.motivation: To establish and characterize the fundamental relationship between the photon index (Γ) and Eddington ratio (λ_Edd) for the radio-quiet quasar population, and to validate accretion trends in the broader context of AGN evolution.
AI.method: Cross-matched XMM-Newton Serendipitous Source Catalog (DR11) with SDSS (DR16) quasar catalog; applied quality filtering and automated spectral reduction to derive photon indices and intrinsic 2–10 keV X-ray luminosities; classified 561 RQ and 81 RL quasars using multiwavelength data; estimated bolometric luminosity and λ_Edd from absorption-corrected X-ray measurements and virial black hole masses.
AI.result: RQ quasars show systematically higher Eddington ratios (peaking at log λ_Edd≈-1.2) and softer spectra (Γ≈2.0). A statistically significant positive correlation between Γ and λ_Edd is found in RQ quasars. λ_Edd increases with redshift and decreases with M_BH for RQ quasars.
AI.conclusion: The Γ–λ_Edd correlation supports disk–corona coupling models; the redshift and mass dependencies of λ_Edd agree with recent results (Aggarwal+2024), highlighting universal accretion trends and providing new insights into the interplay between accretion physics, jet activity, and cosmic quasar evolution.

title: The $M_{\rm BH}$$-$$R_{\rm b}$ relation and the high-mass end of the $M_{\rm BH}$$-$$σ$ relation
comment: 15 pages, 3 figures, 5 tables, accepted for publication in ApJ
summary: Using a sample of 151 galaxies with dynamically measured black hole (BH) masses ($M_{\rm BH}$), we investigate the scaling relations between $M_{\rm BH}$ and the stellar velocity dispersion, $σ$, and, for a subsample of 30 core-Sérsic galaxies, between $M_{\rm BH}$ and the size of the partially depleted core, $R_{\rm b}$. Core-Sérsic galaxies, identified using high-resolution $Hubble ~ Space ~ Telescope$ imaging and spanning both the normal-core $(R_{\rm b}<0.5$ kpc) and large-core ($R_{\rm b}>0.5$ kpc) regimes, define an updated $M_{\rm BH}$$-$$R_{\rm b}$ relation of the form $M_{\rm BH} \propto R_{\rm b}^{1.16 \pm 0.10}$, with an rms scatter of $Δ_{\rm rms} \simeq 0.28$ dex in $\log M_{\rm BH}$. We find that Sérsic and normal-core galaxies together follow a common log-linear $M_{\rm BH}$-$σ$ relation with a slope of $4.95 \pm 0.29$ and a scatter $Δ_{\rm rms} \simeq 0.46$ dex. Deviations from this relation arise at the highest BH masses, where large-core galaxies, including six with direct $M_{\rm BH}$ measurements, drive a significant upturn. We find that these galaxies typically host ultramassive black holes whose masses scale more strongly with $R_{\rm b}$ than $σ$, and lie $\sim (1-4$) $~\times$ the intrinsic scatter (0.39 dex) above the relation defined by Sérsic and normal-core galaxies. The $M_{\rm BH}$$-$$R_{\rm b}$ relation shows $\sim 30$-$47\%$ less scatter in $\log M_{\rm BH}$ than the corresponding $M_{\rm BH}$$-$$σ$ relation for the same sample. We interpret the high-mass upturn in the $M_{\rm BH}$$-$$σ$ diagram as a consequence of successive major, dry mergers, a scenario that naturally explains the observed flattening of the $σ-L_V$ relation at $M_V < -23.5$ mag.

AI.tldr: Core-Sérsic galaxies define an updated M_BH-R_b relation (slope 1.16, scatter 0.28 dex). Large-core galaxies hosting ultramassive BHs deviate upward from the M_BH-σ relation (scatter 0.46 dex). The M_BH-R_b relation shows 30-47% less scatter than M_BH-σ. The high-mass upturn is interpreted as resulting from successive major dry mergers.
AI.motivation: To investigate and update scaling relations between black hole mass and both stellar velocity dispersion (σ) and core size (R_b) using a large sample of dynamically measured BH masses, especially focusing on core-Sérsic galaxies and the high-mass regime.
AI.method: Analyzed scaling relations for 151 galaxies with dynamically measured BH masses. Core-Sérsic galaxies identified via HST imaging were used to define M_BH-R_b relation. Sérsic and normal-core galaxies defined a log-linear M_BH-σ relation. Deviations analyzed for large-core galaxies with ultramassive BHs.
AI.result: M_BH ∝ R_b^(1.16±0.10) with scatter 0.28 dex. M_BH-σ slope = 4.95±0.29 with scatter 0.46 dex. Large-core galaxies lie 1-4× intrinsic scatter above the relation. M_BH-R_b has 30-47% less scatter than M_BH-σ.
AI.conclusion: The high-mass upturn in M_BH-σ is interpreted as a consequence of successive major dry mergers, which also explains the observed flattening of the σ-L_V relation at M_V < -23.5 mag. Core size is a tighter predictor of BH mass than velocity dispersion for the most massive galaxies.

title: Unprecedented Constraints on Gas Flows at High Redshift Using Deep JWST/NIRSpec Observations from the LyC22, EXCELS, and AURORA Surveys
comment: 31 pages, 14 figures, 3 tables, submitted to ApJ
summary: We investigate how low-ionization gas flows in typical star-forming galaxies at $z\sim3$ depend on galaxy intrinsic properties and viewing angle. For this analysis we use JWST/NIRSpec observations of rest-frame near-UV Fe II and Mg II absorption, and rest-frame optical Na D absorption. This study combines galaxies from the LyC22, EXCELS, and AURORA surveys and contains 176, 197, and 315 galaxies, respectively, with Fe II, Mg II, and Na D coverage. Based on both individual and composite spectra, we find no statistically significant correlations between outflow velocity and galaxy properties. However, galaxies with detected outflows tend towards higher stellar masses, SFR, and $Σ_{\rm SFR}$ than those without outflows, suggesting that the two samples are not drawn from the same parent population. Finally, we additionally find that Mg II emission is preferentially detected in galaxies with lower stellar mass and $A_V$, and higher sSFR, consistent with conditions that favor the escape of resonantly scattered line and ionizing continuum radiation. We present the first evidence in $z\sim3$ star-forming galaxies that properties of the absorption lines depend on galaxy inclination, with more face-on systems showing stronger absorption and higher outflow velocities, while inflowing gas is more frequently detected in more highly inclined galaxies. These trends are consistent with observations at $z\lesssim1$ and predictions from cosmological simulations in which galactic winds are launched perpendicular to the galactic disks, while accretion occurs primarily along the disk plane.

AI.tldr: This study analyzes low-ionization gas outflows in z~3 star-forming galaxies using JWST/NIRSpec observations of Fe II, Mg II, and Na D absorption. No strong correlations between outflow velocity and galaxy properties were found, but galaxies with outflows tend to have higher stellar mass, SFR, and Σ_SFR. Mg II emission is preferentially found in lower-mass, lower-A_V, higher-sSFR galaxies. First evidence at z~3 that absorption properties depend on galaxy inclination: face-on systems show stronger absorption and faster outflows, while edge-on systems more frequently show inflowing gas, consistent with wind-perpendicular-to-disk and accretion-along-disk scenarios.
AI.motivation: To understand how low-ionization gas flows (outflows/inflows) in high-redshift (z~3) star-forming galaxies depend on intrinsic galaxy properties and viewing angle, and to test whether the geometric picture of galactic winds (perpendicular to disk) and accretion (along disk plane) seen at lower redshifts holds at z~3.
AI.method: Used JWST/NIRSpec to observe rest-frame near-UV Fe II and Mg II absorption and rest-frame optical Na D absorption in galaxies from the LyC22, EXCELS, and AURORA surveys (N=176, 197, 315 for Fe II, Mg II, Na D respectively). Analyzed individual and composite spectra to correlate outflow properties with galaxy parameters and inclination.
AI.result: No statistically significant correlations between outflow velocity and galaxy intrinsic properties. However, galaxies with detected outflows have higher stellar masses, SFR, and Σ_SFR. Mg II emission is preferentially detected in galaxies with lower stellar mass, lower A_V, and higher sSFR. Absorption line properties depend on inclination: face-on galaxies show stronger absorption and higher outflow velocities; inflowing gas is detected more frequently in highly inclined galaxies.
AI.conclusion: This provides the first evidence at z~3 that galactic outflows and inflows are governed by geometry — outflows are launched perpendicular to galactic disks, while accretion occurs along the disk plane — consistent with lower-redshift observations and cosmological simulations.

title: Supermassive Black Hole Assembly from Heavy Seeds with Dynamical Friction in the BRAHMA Simulations: Implications for JWST, LISA, and the Local Universe
summary: The JWST discoveries of supermassive black holes (BHs) at $z \gtrsim 5$ may provide key insights into their seeding origins. Using new $[18{-}72~\rm Mpc]^3$ BRAHMA cosmological simulations, we investigate how variations in heavy-seed prescriptions, coupled with a subgrid dynamical friction model, shape BH populations at $z \sim 5$ and $z \sim 0$. We consider two "lenient'' seed models, in which all halos containing sufficient dense & metal-poor gas form $\sim10^4$ and $\sim10^5~M_{\odot}$ seeds, and a "strict'' seed model, in which $\sim10^5 M_{\odot}$ seeds form only under additional constraints motivated by direct collapse black hole formation. By $z \sim 5$, all models produce $M_*-M_{\rm BH}$ relations broadly consistent with the observed local Universe for $M_*\gtrsim10^9~M_{\odot}$ galaxies, but only the lenient scenarios generate systems near the upper envelope of the observed local scatter. In galaxies hosting $M_{\rm BH} \sim 10^8$-$10^9~M_{\odot}$ BHs, lenient production of $\sim10^5~M_{\odot}$ seeds also produces multiple overmassive systems with $M_{\rm BH}/M_* \gtrsim 0.01$. Although their growth is dominated by seeding and mergers, these systems reach luminosities of $\sim10^{43}$-$10^{45}\mathrm{erg s^{-1}}$, comparable to those inferred for JWST-detected BHs. As a key observational signature, the lenient seed models yield merger rates of $\gtrsim100\mathrm{yr^{-1}}$ and near-unity local BH occupation fractions even in galaxies with $M_* \lesssim 10^7~M_{\odot}$. In contrast, the strict seed model produces merger rates of only $\sim1\mathrm{yr^{-1}}$ and local occupation fractions of $\lesssim10\%$ for galaxies with $M_* \lesssim 10^8~M_{\odot}$. Future gravitational-wave event rates and measurements of local BH occupation fractions will therefore provide strong constraints on the dominant pathways responsible for high-redshift BH assembly.

AI.tldr: Using BRAHMA cosmological simulations (~18-72 Mpc³), this paper shows that "lenient" heavy-seed models (forming ~10⁴–10⁵ M⊙ BHs in metal-poor gas-rich halos) produce overmassive BHs at z~5 consistent with JWST detections, high merger rates (>100 yr⁻¹), and near-unity BH occupation fractions in dwarf galaxies, while "strict" seed models (motivated by direct collapse) yield low merger rates (~1 yr⁻¹) and <10% occupation fractions in low-mass galaxies, offering observational discriminants via gravitational waves and occupation fraction measurements.
AI.motivation: To understand how different heavy-seed formation pathways for supermassive black holes at high redshift (z≳5) can be distinguished by comparing simulation predictions with JWST observations and local Universe constraints.
AI.method: BRAHMA cosmological simulations (box sizes 18–72 Mpc³) with three seed prescriptions: two lenient models (all halos with sufficient dense metal-poor gas form ~10⁴ M⊙ or ~10⁵ M⊙ seeds) and one strict model (~10⁵ M⊙ seeds only under additional direct-collapse BH conditions), incorporating subgrid dynamical friction for BH dynamics.
AI.result: At z~5, all models match local M*-MBH relations for M*≳10⁹ M⊙ galaxies, but only lenient models produce systems at the upper scatter envelope. Lenient ~10⁵ M⊙ seeds yield overmassive BHs (MBH/M*≳0.01) with luminosities ~10⁴³–10⁴⁵ erg/s, matching JWST-detected BHs. Lenient models give merger rates >100 yr⁻¹ and near-unity occupation fractions in galaxies with M*≲10⁷ M⊙; strict model gives ~1 yr⁻¹ and <10% occupation for M*≲10⁸ M⊙.
AI.conclusion: Future gravitational-wave event rates and local BH occupation fraction measurements can effectively discriminate between lenient and strict heavy-seed scenarios, thereby constraining the dominant seeding pathways for high-redshift BH assembly.

title: SIDM and CDM interpretations of the million-solar-mass lensing perturber JVAS B1938+666-$\mathcal{V}$
summary: A $10^6\,M_\odot$ object has recently been inferred from gravitational imaging of the strong-lensing system JVAS B1938+666, exhibiting an unusually dense inner region embedded within an extended envelope, far exceeding expectations for cold dark matter (CDM) halos. Using gravothermal fluid simulations, we show that such a structure arises naturally in self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) halos evolving into a deep core-collapse phase, where a secondary dense central core forms within an extended profile. The resulting density structure closely matches the inferred properties of the lensing object. We also demonstrate that a similar profile could be reproduced in CDM in the presence of an intermediate-mass black hole, but this requires an early-forming progenitor that subsequently loses $5$ orders of magnitude in mass through tidal stripping by the lens galaxy. Whether such a scenario can be realized in realistic cosmological environments remains an open question.

AI.tldr: A $\sim 10^6\,M_\odot$ dense object in the galaxy-scale strong-lens JVAS B1938+666, initially puzzling for CDM, is naturally explained by self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) undergoing deep core-collapse, forming a secondary dense core within an extended envelope. A CDM+IMBH alternative requires extreme tidal stripping and remains cosmologically questionable.
AI.motivation: To explain the anomalously high central density of a $\sim 10^6\,M_\odot$ object detected via gravitational imaging in the lens system JVAS B1938+666, which cannot be accounted for by standard cold dark matter (CDM) halo profiles.
AI.method: Gravothermal fluid simulations of self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) halos evolving into the deep core-collapse phase, compared with CDM simulations including an intermediate-mass black hole (IMBH) scenario.
AI.result: SIDM core-collapse naturally produces a density structure that closely matches the lensing-inferred properties. CDM with an IMBH can reproduce a similar profile only if the progenitor lost $\sim 10^5$ of its mass via tidal stripping.
AI.conclusion: The observed object is best explained as a deep core-collapse SIDM halo. The CDM+IMBH alternative faces significant plausibility challenges in realistic cosmological environments.

title: Chemical signatures from the first stars embedded in metal-poor gas in galaxies at cosmic dawn
summary: The first generation of stars formed from pristine, neutral hydrogen gas. The most massive of these exploded as supernovae within a few million years of their birth, producing the first heavier elements and leaving distinct chemical signatures of their origin in the surrounding medium. However, chemical abundance studies have so far mainly relied on emission-line measurements, which are luminosity weighted and hence biased towards the most recently formed stars. Here we analyse near-infrared, medium-resolution spectroscopy from the JWST-SPURS program of three UV-bright galaxies at redshifts 7.8, 8.6, and 9.3, within the first 650 to 520 million years after the Big Bang. The chemical abundance patterns of the metal lines detected in absorption hint at extremely metal-poor gas, substantially lower than inferred from the emission lines tracing the central, star-forming regions. Further, they all exhibit super-solar [C/O] abundances, which is also imprinted in the averaged spectrum of a larger set of galaxies at similar redshifts. These results reveal the distinct chemical signatures of the first Population III supernovae explosions.

AI.tldr: Analysis of three UV-bright galaxies at redshifts 7.8–9.3 using JWST-SPURS reveals absorption-line chemical abundance patterns indicating extremely metal-poor gas, super-solar [C/O] ratios, and signatures of the first Population III supernovae, contrasting with emission-line measurements that are biased toward recent star formation.
AI.motivation: Previous chemical abundance studies relied on emission-line measurements, which are luminosity-weighted and biased toward the most recently formed stars, failing to capture the pristine chemical signatures of the first generation (Population III) stars.
AI.method: Near-infrared, medium-resolution spectroscopy from the JWST-SPURS program was used to analyze absorption lines in three UV-bright galaxies at redshifts 7.8, 8.6, and 9.3 (within 520–650 Myr after the Big Bang).
AI.result: The absorption-line chemical abundance patterns reveal extremely metal-poor gas (substantially lower than emission-line inferences), super-solar [C/O] abundances in all three galaxies, and similar signatures in the averaged spectrum of a larger galaxy sample at comparable redshifts.
AI.conclusion: These findings reveal the distinct chemical signatures of the first Population III supernovae explosions, providing direct evidence of primordial stellar nucleosynthesis in the early Universe.

title: Grain Alignment and Dust Evolution Physics with Polarisation (GRADE-POL). II. On the physical basis of Serkowski and super-Serkowski polarisation spectra
summary: Optical-to-near infrared interstellar polarisation, induced by aligned dust grains, generally follows a convex wavelength dependence, known as the Serkowski relation. However, observations in the ultraviolet (UV) and at [mid-]infrared wavelengths indicated that some of the spectra do not follow this relation. Specifically, about 25% show an excess in the degree of polarisation at mid-UV wavelengths ($λ^{-1} > 3\,\rm μm^{-1}$), referred to as the super-Serkowski polarisation. In this study, we re-examine both the Serkowski and super-Serkowski spectra based on the joint effect of paramagnetic relaxation (DG alignment) and radiative torque (RAT) alignment. We used the observational data for HD 30614, HD 204827, HD 37903 and HD 161056 to constrain our modelling. We examined two types of radiation fields: one derived from the scaled interstellar radiation field and another originating from a B-type star. For the super-Serkowski spectra of HD 30614 and HD 204827, our model demonstrates that RAT alignment enhanced by radiation produced from a B-type star below the Lyman limit ($λ=912 Å$) can reasonably explain the observations and that a combination with the DG alignments results in a better fit for $λ^{-1}\geq 5.5\,\rm μm^{-1}$. For the Serkowski spectra in HD 37903 and HD 161056, only RAT alignment by itself under the typical interstellar radiation field above the Lyman limit, within a typical cold neutral medium, can account for the observed spectra, with a combination of a very inefficient DG alignment. The capacity of our model to predict the starlight polarisation spectrum up to from infrared to far-UV is thus a promising tool for interpreting future missions that observe spectrophotometry in the UV bands.

AI.tldr: This paper re-examines Serkowski and super-Serkowski polarisation spectra by modeling the joint effects of paramagnetic relaxation (DG alignment) and radiative torque (RAT) alignment, using observational data from four stars. The model shows that RAT alignment enhanced by B-star radiation below the Lyman limit explains super-Serkowski spectra, while Serkowski spectra are explained by RAT alignment alone under typical interstellar radiation fields. The model can predict starlight polarisation from infrared to far-UV.
AI.motivation: To resolve the discrepancy between the standard Serkowski relation (convex polarisation wavelength dependence) and observed UV/mid-IR polarisation excesses (super-Serkowski) in ~25% of cases, by developing a physical model based on dust grain alignment mechanisms.
AI.method: The authors model the joint effect of paramagnetic relaxation (DG alignment) and radiative torque (RAT) alignment, using observational data for four stars (HD 30614, HD 204827, HD 37903, HD 161056). They test two radiation field types: scaled interstellar radiation field and B-type star radiation. They fit the models to both Serkowski and super-Serkowski spectra.
AI.result: Super-Serkowski spectra (HD 30614, HD 204827) are best explained by RAT alignment enhanced by B-star radiation below the Lyman limit (λ=912 Å), with DG alignment improving fits at λ^{-1}≥5.5 μm^{-1}. Serkowski spectra (HD 37903, HD 161056) are explained by RAT alignment alone under typical interstellar radiation fields above the Lyman limit, with very inefficient DG alignment.
AI.conclusion: The model successfully predicts starlight polarisation spectra from infrared to far-UV, offering a promising tool for interpreting future UV spectrophotometric missions.

title: Beyond the Fundamental Metallicity Relation: galaxy sizes encode the link between inflow and metallicity
comment: 25 pages, 23 figures. Resubmitted to MNRAS after moderate revisions
summary: Gas-phase chemical abundances are key observable consequences of galaxy evolution, being intrinsically tied to galaxy formation histories. Gas metallicity rises with increasing stellar mass ($\mathrm{M_*}$), forming the well-known mass-metallicity relation (MZR). MZR residuals have separately been shown to anti-correlate with star-formation rate (the ``fundamental'' metallicity relation), with gas mass and with optical size, but no single analysis has considered all trends together. We thus perform a combined analysis of all three trends, utilizing optical MaNGA integral field spectroscopy, HI-MaNGA gas masses, and MaNGA DynPop dynamical masses. We estimate inner gas masses for $\sim$1500 star-forming galaxies, finding this to be the most important parameter after $\mathrm{M_*}$ in predicting gas metallicities. We obtain equivalent results for stellar metallicities and gaseous N/O, suggesting that current inner gas masses are intrinsically linked to long-term chemical evolution histories. We show that more compact galaxies have lower dynamical masses, challenging suggestions that deeper gravitational potentials confer higher metallicities. We find a strong correlation between inner gas mass and galaxy size, meaning that short term inflow fluctuations cannot be responsible for the MZR residuals. With chemical evolution models, we show that our results can instead be explained by differences in long-term inflow histories. The earlier inflow histories of compact galaxies lead to lower gas masses and more rapidly declining gas reservoirs at late times, leading to higher metallicities. At fixed stellar mass, galaxy size therefore encodes the link between halo assembly histories, long-term gas inflow histories, current gas reservoirs and metallicity.

AI.tldr: This paper uses MaNGA and HI-MaNGA data to show that inner gas mass is the most important secondary parameter (after stellar mass) in the mass-metallicity relation. More compact galaxies have higher metallicities due to earlier inflow histories leading to lower current gas masses, with galaxy size encoding the link between halo assembly, inflow history, gas reservoirs, and metallicity.
AI.motivation: While MZR residuals are known to anti-correlate with star-formation rate, gas mass, and optical size separately, no single analysis has considered all three trends together. This work performs a combined analysis to understand the underlying physical drivers.
AI.method: Combined analysis using optical MaNGA integral field spectroscopy, HI-MaNGA gas masses, and MaNGA DynPop dynamical masses for ~1500 star-forming galaxies. Inner gas masses were estimated and chemical evolution models were employed to interpret the results.
AI.result: Inner gas mass is the most important parameter after M* for predicting gas metallicities. Equivalent results hold for stellar metallicities and N/O. More compact galaxies have lower dynamical masses (challenging the deeper potential well hypothesis). A strong correlation exists between inner gas mass and galaxy size, ruling out short-term inflow fluctuations as the cause. Chemical evolution models show that differences in long-term inflow histories explain the results.
AI.conclusion: At fixed stellar mass, galaxy size encodes the link between halo assembly histories, long-term gas inflow histories, current gas reservoirs, and metallicity. Earlier inflow histories of compact galaxies lead to lower gas masses and more rapidly declining gas reservoirs at late times, producing higher metallicities.

title: Basis sets and Coulomb resolutions in rotational coordinates
comment: Author-accepted manuscript; see J. Phys. A for final published version
summary: Using generalised Laplacian symmetry operators, we construct basis sets or Coulomb resolutions in several separable coordinate systems, including two R-separable systems. This expands the possible geometries in which basis set construction is feasible, a problem which is relevant to both galactic dynamics and computational chemistry. In particular we derive three basis sets (two in prolate spheroidal and one in cylindrical coordinates) which are expressible in closed-form using a single Jacobi polynomial. We also show how any spherical polar or prolate spheroidal basis set may be transformed into a bispherical or toroidal basis set.

AI.tldr: Using generalised Laplacian symmetry operators, the authors construct new basis sets (Coulomb resolutions) in prolate spheroidal, cylindrical, bispherical, and toroidal coordinate systems, with three closed-form expressions using a single Jacobi polynomial, expanding feasible geometries for galactic dynamics and computational chemistry.
AI.motivation: To expand the range of separable coordinate systems in which basis set construction (Coulomb resolutions) is feasible, addressing a gap relevant to both galactic dynamics and computational chemistry where such basis sets are needed for solving problems in non-spherical geometries.
AI.method: Generalised Laplacian symmetry operators are employed to construct basis sets in several coordinate systems. Three basis sets (two in prolate spheroidal, one in cylindrical) are derived in closed-form using a single Jacobi polynomial. Transformations from spherical polar or prolate spheroidal basis sets to bispherical or toroidal basis sets are demonstrated.
AI.result: Three new closed-form basis sets expressible via a single Jacobi polynomial are derived. Two R-separable systems are included. Transformations linking spherical polar/prolate spheroidal bases to bispherical/toroidal bases are shown.
AI.conclusion: The work expands the geometric possibilities for basis set construction, enabling applications in previously inaccessible coordinate systems important for galactic dynamics and computational chemistry.

title: Galaxy clusters in the VIDEO fields: detection and characterisation in the context of MOONRISE
summary: We analyse the cluster content of the $\sim 4.5 \text{ deg}^{2}$ XMM-LSS and CDFS VIDEO fields which are expected to be partially covered by the upcoming MOONRISE survey. Using AMICO and WaZP photometric redshift-based cluster finders, we construct a sample of $519$ cluster candidates detected by both finders in the redshift range $z = 0.1-3$, including $74$ detections at $z > 1.5$. For all detections, we identify the Brightest Central Galaxy (BCG) and compute a list of probabilistic cluster memberships. Our photometric redshift measurements of the clusters agree well with spectroscopic redshifts from the literature, when available. From ancillary spectroscopic data, we assign $z_\text{spec}$ measurements to $116$ cluster candidates based on their spectroscopic members and to $204$ based on their likely BCGs. We also show that candidates containing Radio-Loud members are efficiently recovered using the prior-based cluster finder PPM. We perform a preliminary analysis of the galaxy content of these candidates, focusing on the Red-Sequence components of their apparent Colour-Magnitude Diagram. By comparing with models of galaxy evolution, we show that this population is consistent with a model of passive evolution with a formation at high redshift, and is already in place at $z = 1.5-2.0$. Finally, our cluster sample is used to evaluate how these clusters would be detected and characterised, according to various MOONRISE strategies. We show that cluster spectroscopic confirmation and characterisation could be efficiently achieved up to $z\sim1.7$ even with the shallowest survey strategy. This open unprecedented insight into the physical properties of high-redshift galaxy clusters and into galaxy formation in dense environments.

AI.tldr: Analysis of 519 galaxy cluster candidates (z=0.1-3, including 74 at z>1.5) in XMM-LSS and CDFS VIDEO fields using AMICO and WaZP finders, demonstrating efficient spectroscopic confirmation up to z~1.7 for future MOONRISE survey and showing red-sequence passive evolution consistent with high-redshift formation.
AI.motivation: To prepare for the upcoming MOONRISE survey by constructing and characterizing a comprehensive sample of galaxy cluster candidates in partially covered fields, evaluating detection and characterization strategies for high-redshift clusters.
AI.method: Used AMICO and WaZP photometric redshift-based cluster finders to detect 519 common cluster candidates; identified BCGs and computed probabilistic memberships; validated photometric redshifts against spectroscopic data; employed PPM prior-based finder for radio-loud member detection; analyzed Colour-Magnitude Diagram red-sequence components with galaxy evolution models.
AI.result: 519 cluster candidates detected (74 at z>1.5); spectroscopic redshifts assigned to 116 via members and 204 via BCGs; efficient radio-loud member recovery with PPM; red-sequence population consistent with passive evolution from high-redshift formation, in place by z=1.5-2.0; spectroscopic confirmation feasible up to z~1.7 even with shallowest MOONRISE strategy.
AI.conclusion: The cluster sample enables unprecedented insight into high-redshift galaxy cluster properties and galaxy formation in dense environments, with MOONRISE capable of efficient spectroscopic characterization up to z~1.7.

title: Feedback in Extragalactic Star Clusters (FEAST): Spectral Energy Distributions and the Physical Properties of Star Clusters in NGC 628 with CIGALE
summary: With Hubble Space Telescope (HST) and James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) observations of NGC~628 spanning 0.3--7.7\,$μ$m, we fit the spectral energy distributions (SEDs) of over 12,000 optically-selected star clusters, emerging young star clusters (eYSCs), and MIRI-selected sources with \textsc{cigale} to derive their ages, masses, extinctions, and dust properties. We find that near-infrared selected eYSC-I (compact Pa$α$ and 3.3,$μ$m PAH emission) and eYSC-II (compact Pa$α$ and diffuse 3.3,$μ$m PAH emssion) sources peak at $\sim$3--5~Myr, where $\sim 12\%$ of the clusters have an $E(B{-}V)>2$, demonstrating the presence of dust-embedded populations as clusters emerge. Further, the distributions of the fractional polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) abundance ($q_{\mathrm PAH}$) and stellar-to-nebular attenuation ratio ($E(B{-}V)_{\rm \star}/E(B{-}V)_{\rm neb}$) suggest an evolutionary sequence in which sources evolve from eYSC-I to eYSC-II as clusters clear their surrounding dust and gas. The photo-dissociation region (PDR) clearing timescale inferred from the ratio of eYSC-I to optically visible stellar clusters is $\sim$4~Myr. Additionally, we find that star clusters in the spiral arms of NGC 628 are preferentially more massive and more dust-reddened than those in inter-arm regions.~Finally, we find that $\sim$65\% of eYSC-I, $\sim$27\% of eYSC-II, and $\sim$40\% of F335M-selected sources coincide with an F770W peak in our MIRI-selected catalog within 4 pixels, confirming that F770W-bright sources preferentially trace the youngest and dustiest regions. Overall, our results highlight the ability of JWST together with \textsc{cigale} model grids to identify and characterize eYSCs during their short-lived embedded phases, and provide constraints on the feedback mechanisms that govern the emergence of stellar clusters.

AI.tldr: Using HST + JWST observations of NGC~628 (0.3–7.7 μm), this study fits SEDs of ~12,000 star clusters and emerging young star clusters (eYSCs) with CIGALE to derive ages, masses, extinction, and dust properties. eYSC-I and eYSC-II peak at ~3–5 Myr, ~12% have E(B-V)>2. An evolutionary sequence from eYSC-I → eYSC-II is inferred via PAH abundance and attenuation ratios. PDR clearing timescale ~4 Myr. Spiral arm clusters are more massive and dust-reddened. ~65% eYSC-I, ~27% eYSC-II, ~40% F335M sources align with F770W peaks, tracing youngest/dustiest regions.
AI.motivation: To characterize the evolutionary stages and timescales of embedded young star clusters emerging from their natal dust/gas, and to understand feedback mechanisms governing cluster emergence, using multi-wavelength (UV–MIRI) observations.
AI.method: SED fitting of ~12,000 optically-selected clusters, eYSCs (eYSC-I: compact Paα+compact 3.3μm PAH; eYSC-II: compact Paα+diffuse 3.3μm PAH), and MIRI-selected sources using CIGALE. Analyzed age, mass, E(B-V), q_PAH, stellar-to-nebular attenuation ratio; spatial correlation with MIRI F770W peaks; compared arm vs. inter-arm populations.
AI.result: eYSC-I and eYSC-II peak at ~3–5 Myr; ~12% have E(B-V)>2. q_PAH and E(B-V)_star/E(B-V)_neb distributions suggest eYSC-I → eYSC-II evolution. PDR clearing timescale ~4 Myr. Spiral arm clusters more massive and dust-reddened. 65% eYSC-I, 27% eYSC-II, 40% F335M sources match F770W peaks within 4 pixels.
AI.conclusion: JWST + CIGALE can robustly identify and characterize eYSCs in their short embedded phases. The results provide observational constraints on feedback processes (e.g., PDR clearing) and evolutionary pathways of young star clusters.

title: Direct detection of cool molecular gas in a star-forming galaxy at $z=7.31$
comment: Accepted for publication in MNRAS. Main text: 17 pages, 6 figures
summary: We investigate the molecular gas content and interstellar medium (ISM) conditions of REBELS-25, a massive, star-forming galaxy at $z=7.31$. Deep VLA Q-band and ALMA Band 3 observations reveal CO(3-2) and CO(7-6) emission (both at $\sim3.5σ$), and provide an upper limit on [C I](2-1). From the CMB-corrected CO(3-2) flux-representing the highest-redshift detection of a low-$J$ CO transition to date-we derive a molecular gas mass of $M_{\rm mol}=(1.0\pm0.4)\times10^{11}\,(α_{\rm CO}/(3\,$M$_{\odot}$(K$\,$\kms$\,$pc$^2)^{-1}))\,$M$_{\odot}$, directly confirming the presence of a very massive gas reservoir only $\simeq700\,$Myr after the Big Bang. This implies an extreme gas fraction of $f_{\rm gas}\simeq0.95$, a gas-to-dust ratio of $δ_{\rm GDR}\simeq6\times10^2$, and a depletion timescale of $τ_{\rm dep}\simeq1.2\,$Gyr, broadly consistent with extrapolated scaling relations for main-sequence galaxies at lower redshift. Using the radiative transfer code TUNER, we self-consistently model CO and dust continuum emission in the context of the significant CMB background, constraining ISM properties and recovering $M_{\rm mol}= (1.8^{+1.0}_{-0.9})\times10^{11}\,$M$_{\odot}$, independent of assumptions about $r_{31}$ and $α_{\rm CO}$. We further discuss the use of alternative molecular gas tracers at early epochs. Combining CO and [C II] measurements, we infer an empirical [C II]-to-H$_2$ conversion factor of $α_{\rm [C II]}=(60\pm25)\,$M$_{\odot}$/L$_{\odot}$, suggesting [C II] remains a viable molecular gas tracer in the Epoch of Reionization. These results demonstrate the detectability of low-$J$ CO emission even at $z>7$, paving the way for next-generation facilities, and provide critical insights into the rapid mass assembly of galaxies during the first billion years of cosmic history.

AI.tldr: This paper reports the highest-redshift detection of low-J CO emission (CO(3-2)) in REBELS-25 at z=7.31, confirming a massive molecular gas reservoir (~1-2×10¹¹ M☉) only 700 Myr after the Big Bang. The galaxy shows extreme gas fraction (~95%), and the study demonstrates that CO and [C II] remain viable molecular gas tracers in the Epoch of Reionization.
AI.motivation: To investigate the molecular gas content and ISM conditions of REBELS-25, a massive star-forming galaxy at z=7.31, in order to understand the rapid mass assembly of galaxies during the first billion years of cosmic history.
AI.method: Deep VLA Q-band and ALMA Band 3 observations targeting CO(3-2), CO(7-6), and [C I](2-1) emission, combined with radiative transfer modeling using TUNER to self-consistently model CO and dust continuum emission under significant CMB background.
AI.result: Detection of CO(3-2) and CO(7-6) at ~3.5σ, deriving molecular gas mass M_mol=(1.0±0.4)×10¹¹ M☉ (assuming α_CO=3) from CO(3-2), or M_mol=(1.8^{+1.0}_{-0.9})×10¹¹ M☉ from radiative transfer modeling. Extreme gas fraction f_gas~0.95, gas-to-dust ratio δ_GDR~6×10², depletion time τ_dep~1.2 Gyr. Empirical [C II]-to-H₂ conversion factor α_[C II]=(60±25) M☉/L☉.
AI.conclusion: Low-J CO emission is detectable at z>7, confirming a massive gas reservoir early in cosmic history. CO and [C II] remain viable molecular gas tracers in the Epoch of Reionization, paving the way for next-generation facilities to study galaxy mass assembly in the early universe.

title: The ultra low-frequency spectral properties of bright extended radio galaxies in the 3CRR catalogue
summary: Context. Active galactic nuclei (AGN) jets are fundamental drivers of galaxy evolution, injecting kinetic energy into their environments. The large-scale morphology and spectral properties of these radio galaxies are consequences of complex particle acceleration, energy loss, and absorption processes. While the shape of the synchrotron spectrum encodes the plasma's energetic history, understanding the physics of particle acceleration and duty cycles has historically been limited by a lack of well-resolved observations at ultra-low frequencies (< 100 MHz), where the oldest cosmic ray electron populations are traced. Aims. This study aims to perform the first comprehensive multi-frequency analysis of bright extended radio galaxies down to 58 MHz. The goal is to study electron acceleration mechanisms, accurately measure the low-frequency spectral shape, and constrain the injection index for a sample of Fanaroff-Riley (FR) I and II galaxies using spectral ageing models. Methods. Utilising new 58 MHz observations from the LOFAR Low Band Antenna (LBA) combined with LOFAR High Band Antenna (HBA; 144 MHz) and Rapid ASKAP Continuum Survey (RACS, 887 MHz & 943.5 MHz & 1367.5 MHz) data, a sub-sample of 22 extended sources from the 3CRR catalogue was selected, requiring the largest angular size to be at least 2.5'. The analysis involves constructing detailed spectral index maps and utilising radio colour-colour diagrams to interpret spectral shapes and constrain ageing model parameters across the radio lobes. Results. This study presents the ultra-low frequency spectral index maps for this sample. For FR I galaxies, spectral indices range from ~0.5 near the core (consistent with first-order Fermi acceleration) to > 1.0 in the lobes. For FR II galaxies, hotspots exhibit steep low-frequency spectra (0.5 - 0.9), suggesting complex acceleration or absorption effects.

AI.tldr: This study presents the first comprehensive multi-frequency analysis of 22 bright extended radio galaxies down to 58 MHz using LOFAR LBA, HBA, and RACS data. It constructs spectral index maps and uses radio colour-colour diagrams to study particle acceleration, measure low-frequency spectral shapes, and constrain injection indices for FR I and II galaxies via spectral ageing models.
AI.motivation: AGN jets are key drivers of galaxy evolution, but understanding particle acceleration physics and duty cycles has been limited by a lack of well-resolved ultra-low frequency observations (< 100 MHz), where the oldest cosmic ray electron populations are traced.
AI.method: Utilized new LOFAR LBA (58 MHz), LOFAR HBA (144 MHz), and RACS (887, 943.5, 1367.5 MHz) data. Selected a sub-sample of 22 extended sources from the 3CRR catalogue (largest angular size ≥ 2.5'). Constructed spectral index maps and radio colour-colour diagrams to interpret spectral shapes and constrain ageing model parameters.
AI.result: Presented ultra-low frequency spectral index maps. For FR I galaxies: spectral indices range from ~0.5 near the core (consistent with first-order Fermi acceleration) to > 1.0 in lobes. For FR II galaxies: hotspots exhibit steep low-frequency spectra (0.5–0.9), suggesting complex acceleration or absorption effects.
AI.conclusion: The low-frequency observations enable detailed spectral modelling of electron populations, providing constraints on injection indices and ageing mechanisms in FR I and II radio galaxies, with implications for understandingAGN feedback and particle acceleration history.

title: Centrally concentrated star formation in young clusters II: Jet feedback
comment: Data products associated with this work will be made publicly available through the American Museum of Natural History Digital Library after the paper is accepted for publication
summary: Protostellar jets are one of the earliest forms of stellar feedback, but their impact on star formation and cluster assembly in centrally concentrated molecular clouds remains poorly understood. We study how protostellar jets affect the star formation efficiency, the temporal variability of star formation, star cluster structure, and the early dynamical state of centrally concentrated, newly forming star clusters using the Torch star cluster formation framework. We adopt a centrally concentrated initial cloud model with mass M = 2.5 x 10^3 solar masses and compare six pairs of simulations with and without protostellar jets, supplemented by one additional higher resolution pair of simulations. We analyze our simulations using global star formation diagnostics together with structural and dynamical measures of the stellar population. Models with jet feedback achieve star formation efficiencies of 12-16%, while the corresponding models without jets yield higher efficiencies of 19-33%. Jets also cause star formation to occur in discrete bursts rather than continuously, to produce more extended and substructured stellar systems, and to leave behind stellar populations that are less tightly bound and have higher virial parameters. In our centrally concentrated initial conditions, runs with jets form stellar systems that better reproduce the observed range of the projected structural parameter Q_2D in young clusters than runs without jets, indicating that protostellar jets are an important early feedback channel even in centrally concentrated clouds that regulates star formation efficiencies and shapes the emerging cluster structure.

AI.tldr: Protostellar jets regulate star formation efficiency (12-16% vs 19-33% without jets), cause episodic rather than continuous star formation, produce more extended/substructured clusters, and result in less bound stellar populations with higher virial parameters. Jets help simulations better match observed young cluster structures.
AI.motivation: To understand how protostellar jets affect star formation efficiency, temporal variability, cluster structure, and dynamics in centrally concentrated molecular clouds, as their role in early stellar feedback remains poorly understood.
AI.method: Used Torch star cluster formation framework with a centrally concentrated initial cloud model (M = 2.5×10³ M☉), comparing six simulation pairs with and without protostellar jets plus one higher-resolution pair, analyzed via global star formation diagnostics and structural/dynamical measures.
AI.result: Jets reduce star formation efficiency (12-16% vs 19-33%), induce episodic bursts, produce more extended/substructured systems with higher virial parameters and lower binding; jet simulations better reproduce observed Q_2D structural parameters in young clusters.
AI.conclusion: Protostellar jets are an important early feedback channel even in centrally concentrated clouds, regulating star formation efficiencies and shaping young cluster structure.
